grammarNote.title: 💡 Dropping the 'i' (い)
grammarNote.content: For i-adjectives, you must drop the final 'い' before adding the conjugation. For example, the Te-form is 'おいしくて' (oishikute), which you can use to connect thoughts: 京都の湯豆腐は美味しくて、温かいです (The yudofu in Kyoto is delicious and warm).

flexions.japanese: 美味しくなかったです

grammarNote.title: 💡 Na-adjectives act like nouns
grammarNote.content: Unlike i-adjectives, na-adjectives use 'desu' (です) or 'da' (だ) to conjugate. When connecting sentences, their Te-form is simply 'で' (de). Example: 箱根の旅館は静かで、きれいです (The inn in Hakone is quiet and beautiful).

flexions.japanese: 静かじゃなかったです

grammarNote.title: ⚠️ The Ultimate Exception
grammarNote.content: 'いい' (ii) means good, but the moment you conjugate it, it reverts to its older form 'よい' (yoi). So it becomes 'よくない' (yokunai), not 'いくない' (ikunai). Example: 下北沢の古着屋はとてもいいです (The thrift shops in Shimokitazawa are very good).
